links.outcome: Discrimination of externally developed TKI failure model on local French cohort
links.effect: Model 1 hazard ratios were 1.2 (intermediate) and 2.0 (high) vs 5.4 and 12.1 in the original Chinese cohort; all AUCs <0.68.
links.quote: Despite this significant result, the hazard ratios obtained using the low-risk group as reference were low compared with those reported by Zhang et al.: 1.2 (95% CI: 0.9–1.7, p = 0.2) vs . 5.4 (95% CI: 4.1–7.2, p < 0.001) for the intermediate-risk group and 2.0 (95% CI: 1.2–3.2, p = 0.006) vs . 12.1 (95% CI: 8.8–16.6, p < 0.001) for the high-risk group.

links.outcome: Differences between development and local cohorts and their effect on model performance
links.effect: French cohort was older (58 vs 40 years), had higher hemoglobin, and more 2G-TKI use; model did not discriminate risk groups effectively.
links.quote: The key differences identified between the Chinese and French cohorts (age, baseline hemoglobin levels, and treatment regimens) likely influenced the model performance.

links.outcome: Performance after local recalibration and re-optimization of model using French data
links.effect: Model 2 recalibration gave HR 1.5 and 2.1; Model 3 gave HR 1.7 and 2.1, still below original 5.4 and 12.1; AUCs remained <0.68 with no significant improvement.
links.quote: However, the overall predictive performance remained inferior to that reported for the original Chinese cohort.

links.outcome: Generalization of a predictive model to a new population
links.effect: Model developed in a Chinese cohort did not discriminate risk groups effectively in the French cohort; HRs much lower than reported.
links.quote: In conclusion, our study demonstrates the limitations of directly transposing predictive models developed in ethnically or clinically distinct populations and also offers new insights that could advance personalized treatment strategies in CP-CML.

links.outcome: Optimism bias from evaluating recalibrated models on the same dataset used to build them
links.effect: Models 2 and 3 were calibrated and evaluated on the same French dataset, risking overfitting; authors call for a fully independent validation cohort.
links.quote: Also, it should be noted that Models 2 and 3 were calibrated with the same dataset used for the ROC comparisons.

links.outcome: Comparison of new models against existing ELTS score on same data
links.effect: All AUCs (ELTS and Models 1-3) were <0.68; Model 3 tended to be slightly better but the difference was not significant.
links.quote: Model 3 tended to be slightly more effective, but the difference was not significant.

links.outcome: predictive performance after local recalibration and model optimization
links.effect: AUC values were all <0.68 across Models 1, 2, 3, and ELTS regardless of first-line TKI; Model 3 tended to be slightly more effective, but the difference was not significant.
links.quote: To compare the predictive performance of the ELTS and Models 1, 2, and 3 scores, we calculated their AUC values, which were all <0.68 (Fig. 4A–C ), regardless of the first-line TKI (Fig. 4D–I ).

screen.practice: local validation and recalibration of predictive model before use
screen.reason: The study conducts an external validation and recalibration/reconstruction of a predictive risk model developed in a Chinese cohort on a French real-world cohort, demonstrating failure of generalizability and evaluating population-specific adaptation.
